key_insight: LesionAgent proposes a training-free LLM agent for tracking tumors across CT scans and assessing treatment response. It aims to connect image-analysis capabilities with the longitudinal reasoning and clinical-rule checks used by radiologists.
problem_solved: Detecting or segmenting tumors is not enough: longitudinal assessment also requires deciding which findings are lesions, matching them across visits, and determining whether new findings indicate disease progression.
method: Use an LLM agent to guide end-to-end assessment of longitudinal CT scans without task-specific training.
Link lesion identification and tracking across time with treatment-response assessment.
Check lesion-level decisions against clinical-guideline rules.
impact: The approach suggests a way to turn specialized imaging models into a clinically structured workflow through agentic reasoning. The supplied abstract is truncated, so performance and validation details cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: CT timeline linking the same lesions across successive scans.
Workflow diagram: CT scans → LLM agent and imaging tools → response assessment.
Clinical-rule checklist beside lesion-matching and progression decisions.
Highlighted new lesion illustrating why detection alone does not establish progression.
paper_title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
paper_authors: Maximilian Rokuss, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Alejandro Lozano, Benjamin Hamm, Yannick Kirchhoff
